transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm just here because... I feel like I'm always up and moving, you know? Like, even on a quiet day, I'm just bouncing around. I'll go from checking my garden club list to digging through my knitting bag, and then I'm looking at travel papers... all before I've really finished any one of those things. It's just constant activity, and I wanted to talk to someone about it.
Has this feeling of constant movement and bouncing between tasks been something you've experienced since childhood, or is it a more recent change?

It's definitely not a recent change. I've been this way pretty much my whole life. Even back in grade school... well, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl, but just scattered. I was always losing my papers, talking out of turn, and wiggling around in my seat before I even finished my schoolwork. So, yes, it's been going on since I was little.
How do these difficulties with staying focused and moving between tasks impact your daily life, work, or relationships today?

Well, it's... it's started causing some real strain lately. Mostly at home with my husband, and down at the community center where I volunteer. It's just getting to the point where they feel like they can't really count on me to keep our plans straight. Like, someone always has to check behind me to make sure I actually finished what I said I was going to do, or that I didn't double-book myself. It's frustrating for them, and honestly, it's frustrating for me too.

inference_history.note: Initial candidates based on restlessness, distractibility, and constant multitasking/hyperactivity, suggesting hypomania/mania, ADHD, or anxiety.

Symptoms have been continuously present since childhood with classic signs of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, ruling out episodic mood disorders (F30.0, F31.0, F31.1) and generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) as the primary diagnosis.
